summary: Iteration 33 (extraction of routes/events.py + routes/members.py + routes/auth_email_flows.py from server.py + 'Pending password setup' badge/filter/resend on Admin → Members): ALL 25 backend tests PASS, and ALL UI elements verified live. Refactor 1 (auth_email_flows): set-password bogus token → 400 'Invalid or already-used token'; forgot-password returns ok=true for both known and unknown emails (enumeration-safe); reset-password bogus token → 400 'Invalid or already-used reset link.'; change-password unauth → 401, wrong-current → 400 'Current password is incorrect', correct → 200 and new password works for login (then restored). _send_set_password_email._impl shim correctly delegates to routes/auth_email_flows.send_set_password_email so bulk-import / apply-approval / resend-link continue to send the welcome email. Refactor 2 (events): GET /events (list/upcoming/include_sub_events), GET /events/{id} (404), admin POST/PUT (cancelled toggle stamps cancelled_at + clears on revert)/DELETE all work; sub-events + rsvps subresources work; member 403 on POST/PUT/DELETE. Refactor 3 (members): GET /members (q + city filters), GET /members/{id} (404), /members-new, /members-birthdays (Feb 29 next-birthday computation present), PUT /members/{id}/status (sets deceased_at stamp, clears on non-deceased status, member→403). public_user now exposes pending_set_password:bool. Feature 4 (resend + badge): POST /api/admin/members/{id}/resend-set-password — member→403, unknown user→404, admin→200 with {ok, sent, email} sets pending_set_password=true; second resend also returns 200 (older tokens invalidated). UI verified live: filter-pending-setpw toolbar button shows '2 pending password setup', clicking it shrinks the table from 14 → 2 rows (all of which contain a pending-setpw-<id> amber badge in the name cell + a resend-setpw-<id> button in the actions cell); clicking again restores 14 rows.
critical_code_review_comments: Refactor is clean: events.py (97 lines), members.py (107 lines), auth_email_flows.py (162 lines) each have a single responsibility and a thin register(api, **deps) signature. server.py shrinks from 7654 to 7448 lines (-206 net). The injected dependencies (event_out, public_user, admin_tab_dep, hash/verify_password, iso/now_utc, resend_sdk, logger) cleanly avoid circular imports.

The _send_set_password_email back-compat shim at server.py:488-498 is correctly wired: after routes_auth_email_flows.register(...) runs at line 7403, line 7418 sets _send_set_password_email._impl = register.send_set_password_email. The shim logs and returns False if called before registration (defensive — verified that all callers go through the shim, none reach the helper before registration since registration is at module top-level after the FastAPI app exists).

Pydantic v2 EmailStr validation means /auth/forgot-password rejects 'foo@nowhere.test'-style synthetic addresses with a 422 — enumeration safety still holds because real-looking unknown emails still return {ok:true} (verified with nobody-<hex>@example.com). Not a bug but worth noting for future test authors.

POST /admin/members/{id}/resend-set-password correctly: (1) invalidates older unused tokens via update_many used=true + invalidated_by='resend', (2) creates a 7-day token, (3) sets pending_set_password=true on the user, (4) sends via _send_set_password_email (Resend), (5) returns {ok, sent:bool, email}. 503 is returned when RESEND_API_KEY is missing — sandbox has it configured so live test got sent:true.

Frontend Admin.jsx visibleMembers / pendingOnly / pendingCount logic at lines 746-748 is correct. The 'filter-pending-setpw' button only renders when pendingCount > 0 (good UX). The pending-setpw-<id> amber badge and resend-setpw-<id> button are both rendered conditionally on m.pending_set_password.

Pre-existing phase_g/phase_h test failures (12 fail, 8 error) are UNRELATED to this iteration — they test the apply/application flow that now requires a password field plus a renamed event ('Sip and Paint' → 'Sip & Paint'). These would need their own iteration to refresh — flagging for future cleanup, not as a regression of iter33.
